description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1 (AMEND 5b). Sends '/clear' over the resolved host driver's driver channel (stream-json stdin) to the running Claude Code process behind agent_instance_id -- fire-and-forget, this call does not read or await the resulting turn. Optional park=true additionally drives the ledger row from live/idle/overdue to parked (L3 rule 2, steward direction) -- the ONLY writer of that lifecycle edge. Only available on hosts whose driver provides a driver channel (currently 'headless' and 'tmux'); the degenerate 'operator' driver, and a headless/tmux process this build's memory no longer tracks (e.g. after a restart), both refuse with unsupported_on_host rather than silently doing nothing.
embedding_description: Nuke a fleet session's memory back to zero via '/clear' -- every prior turn is gone, unrecoverable, with an optional park flag to retire the ledger row too. The panic-button verb: context is corrupted, or the operator wants a hard reset. Nothing here reduces size gently -- that's compact_session's job. terminate_session ends the process itself, not just its memory.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: lifecycle_state (the row's state after this call) and parked (true only when park=true was passed and the live/idle/overdue -> parked transition actually landed).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call is fire-and-forget: a clean result confirms the command was sent over the driver channel, not that the target session has finished processing it.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Reads the managed_session ledger row, refuses on a terminal lifecycle_state, resolves the row's host driver, and sends '/clear' over its driver_channel() -- a fixed sequence, no retry loop.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. lifecycle_state_conflict: the row is already terminated/retired -- terminal rows never receive driver-channel commands. unsupported_on_host: the row's host has no driver in this build, or its driver has no live driver channel for this host_ref (the degenerate 'operator' driver, or a headless process spawned before a restart wiped this build's in-memory tracking).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For unsupported_on_host, use the manual equivalent for that session (e.g. typing /clear directly if it is an operator-attended session) -- this verb has no fallback path, by design, to avoid a silent no-op.
